paragraphs: Shimon ben Guda–Gudaʿ. (A tanna cited in a baraita.)

In [Avodah Zarah 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.32a.9), Shimon ben Gudaʿ testified before Rabban Gamliel’s son that Rabban Gamliel had drunk from it in Akko. Tosafot there writes that he testified before Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel, the brother of R' Shimon ben Gamliel, Rabbi’s father. The Tosefta there, chapter 5, however, explicitly says that he testified before the son of Rabban Gamliel the Elder, and gives the name Shimon ben Gudya. The Gemara there also says: “Alternatively, Gudaʿ is one person and Guda is another” (two tannaim).[^1]

notes.text: The distinct spellings גודא, גודע and גודיא are retained as Guda, Gudaʿ and Gudya. לחוד distinguishes the two rather than saying “alone.” No object such as “wine” is added to Hyman’s ממנו, “from it.” ואבע״א introduces the alternative explanation. The reported genealogy makes R' Shimon ben Gamliel Rabbi’s father. The full רבי in Hyman supports the standalone title “Rabbi”; the abbreviated רשב״ג is not assigned a full honorific from general identity knowledge.

The William Davidson Hebrew paragraph at Avodah Zarah 32a:9 explicitly has Rabban Gamliel in both relevant occurrences. The Vilna Tosafot paragraph beginning אבל בנו מודי ליה explicitly has רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, supporting Rabbi Chanina in that report, while its Shimon ben Gamliel honorific remains abbreviated and is rendered R'. The Machon Mamre Tosefta, Avodah Zarah 5:4, has Shimon ben Gudya testifying before Rabban Gamliel’s son *in the name of* Rabban Gamliel the Elder; Hyman instead says before the Elder’s son. The English retains Hyman’s asserted contrast and records this wording difference, without equating the two generations or silently rewriting his text.
